title: Harborview Offshore Wind Transmission Corridor
description: A proposed transmission corridor for a 1.2 GW offshore wind project has drawn competing claims over grid reliability, ratepayer costs, fishing grounds, and coastal habitat protections.

contestedQuestions.question: Will the corridor materially improve regional grid reliability?
Are projected ratepayer costs justified by long-term benefits?
Are fisheries and coastal habitat protections adequate?

stakeholders.name: State Energy Office
stakeholders.positionSummary: Argues the corridor is needed to connect offshore generation and reduce peak-season reliability risk.

stakeholders.name: Harbor Fishermen Alliance
stakeholders.positionSummary: Warns that cable routing and construction windows could disrupt trawling grounds and port revenue.

stakeholders.name: Coastal Ratepayer Council
stakeholders.positionSummary: Supports cleaner energy goals but wants stronger bill-impact guarantees and public cost reporting.

title: AI Hiring Audit Rule
description: A proposed AI hiring audit rule would require employers using automated screening tools to test for disparate impact, disclose tool use to applicants, and keep audit records for regulators.

contestedQuestions.question: Would the audit rule materially reduce algorithmic discrimination in hiring?
Are compliance costs proportionate for smaller employers?
Are applicant disclosure requirements clear enough?

stakeholders.name: Equal Opportunity Office
stakeholders.positionSummary: Says automated hiring tools need auditable safeguards and applicant notice.

stakeholders.name: Employer Software Coalition
stakeholders.positionSummary: Supports clearer rules but warns that broad audit mandates could slow adoption and raise costs.

stakeholders.name: Worker Rights Network
stakeholders.positionSummary: Wants independent audits, applicant appeal rights, and public reporting on high-volume screening tools.

title: Central Bank Rate Hold
description: The central bank held its benchmark rate steady while signaling that inflation progress, labor-market cooling, and credit conditions will determine whether cuts begin later this year.

contestedQuestions.question: Is inflation progress strong enough to justify rate cuts soon?
Is the labor market weakening enough to change policy?
Are households still under meaningful credit stress?

stakeholders.name: Central Bank Policy Committee
stakeholders.positionSummary: Wants confidence that inflation is moving toward target without triggering unnecessary labor-market damage.

stakeholders.name: Household Borrowers
stakeholders.positionSummary: Face elevated mortgage, auto, and credit-card borrowing costs while waiting for possible rate cuts.

stakeholders.name: Market Investors
stakeholders.positionSummary: Are pricing the likely timing and size of rate cuts into bond yields and equity valuations.

title: Dry Creek Water Allocation Plan
description: A drought-year water allocation plan would prioritize municipal reserves and river flows while cutting some irrigation deliveries, prompting competing claims about public health, farm income, and ecosystem protection.

contestedQuestions.question: Should municipal reserves receive priority over irrigation deliveries?
Are farm income losses adequately mitigated?
Are river-flow protections sufficient for fish and tribal water interests?

stakeholders.name: River Basin Authority
stakeholders.positionSummary: Says reserve thresholds and flow targets are needed to manage a severe drought year.

stakeholders.name: Dry Creek Growers
stakeholders.positionSummary: Warn that irrigation cuts will force acreage reductions and seasonal layoffs.

stakeholders.name: Tribal River Council
stakeholders.positionSummary: Argues minimum flows are a baseline obligation, not a discretionary environmental add-on.
